p: Obavva belonged to the Holaya community. Her husband, Kahale Mudda Hanuma, was the guard of a watchtower in the rocky fort of Chitradurga, which the troops of Hyder Ali besieged during the reign of Madakari Nayaka. As the story is told, a chance sighting of a man entering the fort through a hole in the rocks gave Hyder Ali the plan of sending his soldiers in by the same way.

The guard on duty near the hole had gone home for his meal. When he wanted water, Obavva went to fetch it in a pot from a pond near the hole, halfway up the hill, and there saw the soldiers trying to enter. She struck each on the head with the pestle as he came through and quietly moved the body aside, so that those behind suspected nothing. Mudda Hanuma returned to find her standing with the bloodstained pestle among the enemy dead.

She was found dead later the same day, either from shock or killed by enemy soldiers. Her act saved the fort on that occasion, but Madakari Nayaka could not withstand Hyder Ali's attack in 1779, when Chitradurga was lost to him.

In Karnataka she is honoured beside Abbakka Rani, Keladi Chennamma and Kittur Chennamma as one of the foremost women warriors of the state. Since 2021 the Government of Karnataka has celebrated 11 November as Onake Obavva Jayanti. A sports stadium in Chitradurga bears her name, and a statue of her by the sculptor Ashok Gudigar stands in front of the District Commissioner's office there. Her deed is shown in a song sequence of the film Nagarahavu, directed by Puttanna Kanagal, in which the actress Jayanthi played her, and in the 2019 Kannada film Chitradurgada Onake Obavva, with the actress Tara in the role.

notes: Short article (about 300 words of substance): two sections only.
The article tells the story flatly, with no source; I added 'As the story is told' once, in keeping with the existing description's 'is said to have'.
The article writes 'Hyder Ali (1754-1779)', which are not his life or reign dates as usually given; I used only the 1779 fall of the fort. No date is given for Obavva's deed itself.
